intro.title: Write a cancellable async task abstraction
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable JavaScript function called a 'cancellable async task abstraction.' This function will allow you to start an asynchronous operation, like fetching data, and cancel it before it completes if needed. You will learn to use core JavaScript concepts such as Promises, async/await, and state flags to control task execution. By the end, you will have a practical tool for managing long-running or unnecessary async tasks in your applications. This lesson is designed for beginners, focusing on clear, step-by-step implementation without external libraries.
intro.usecase: Cancellable async tasks are essential for responsive user interfaces where users need to interrupt ongoing operations. In search interfaces, users expect to cancel a slow search query when typing new characters. In dashboard applications with data refreshes, users should be able to stop a pending update when navigating away. File upload components also require cancellation to let users abort transfers before completion. This pattern prevents wasted resources and improves user control over long-running operations.
